inputs.share_count_basis: Basic shares in issue net of shares held under the share award scheme at 30 June 2026 (2,796.65m issued less ~26.2m award-scheme treasury = 2,770.7m weighted) plus 0.4m dilutive awarded shares (H1 FY2026 interim note 7). The EUR1.5bn zero-coupon 2029 Convertible Bonds (122.6m conversion shares at HKD99.80) are EXCLUDED from the count because they are out of the money at HKD77.95 and are carried instead as debt at full principal (RMB11,914m) in net debt -- counting them in both places would double-charge. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. No buybacks in H1 FY2026 (FY2025 RMB1,952m, FY2024 RMB844m); EUR300m of CB proceeds remains reserved for buybacks, so the flat count is partly funded.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, consolidated statement of changes in equity / note 26(f): equity-settled share-based payment transactions RMB324m (FY2024 RMB275m). No net-share-settlement tax withholding line exists (HK share award scheme is funded by on-market purchases), so equity-award taxes are 0.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are RMB'million throughout (every primary statement is headed RMB'million); price is the HKEX quote in HKD. All flows, net debt and bridge items are modelled in CNY and per-share values converted CNY->HKD at 1.1724 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16 close). Parity check via USD crosses: USDHKD 7.8479 / USDCNY 6.6768 = 1.1754, a 0.26% tie, confirming direction (1 CNY = 1.17 HKD). No dual listing exists for a direct parity check. Note refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: WACC = cost of equity (the group is net cash; debt is a zero-coupon CB and short-dated RMB bills). Built in RMB: China 10Y government bond ~1.8-2.0% + equity risk premium ~6.5% x beta ~1.0 + ~1.5pp for an HK-listed, founder-controlled (Ding family ~53%) Chinese consumer name with offshore minority holders = 10.0%. Applied identically in all three scenarios; scenario risk lives in the flows, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2025 'Payments of lease liabilities' RMB4,700m (financing section; capital and interest elements combined -- lease interest was RMB334m in note 3) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (5.9% of revenue). Lease liabilities (RMB8,462m at 31 Dec 2025, RMB7,854m at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Adj EBITDA is pre-IFRS-16 (adds back right-of-use depreciation RMB4,787m) and the D&A path is ex-right-of-use (PPE depreciation RMB1,548m + intangibles amortisation RMB177m = 2.15% of revenue), so the lease is charged exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are attributable-only. NCI (FILA China ~15% external, DESCENTE and KOLON SPORT JVs ~40-46% external) took RMB2,074m of FY2025 profit, ~14% of operating profit after associates, and 16.6% in H1 FY2026 as the 'all other brands' segment grew 44%. That share is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax + NCI leakage: 1 - (1 - 28% cash tax) x (1 - 15-17% NCI) = ~39-40%. Calibration: FY2025 EBIT on this build ~RMB19.0bn x (1 - 38.8%) = RMB11.6bn vs adjusted attributable profit RMB12.4bn less ~RMB0.7bn after-tax/after-NCI net finance income = RMB11.7bn -- ties within 1%. No separate NCI deduction in the bridge (that would charge it twice). Caveat: part of the group cash sits in non-wholly-owned subsidiaries (notably FILA) and is not 100% attributable; unquantified and not deducted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the non-US adaptations (RMB/HKD currency split, IFRS-16 leases treatment B, NCI folded into leakage, excluded-income matching assets). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US: consumer' -- ANTA is a vertically integrated branded sportswear operator (ANTA, FILA China, DESCENTE, KOLON SPORT, JACK WOLFSKIN, MAIA ACTIVE), not a financial, REIT or holdco, and no prior valuation or MEMORY.md entry exists. Its two big equity-accounted stakes are valued separately in the equity_bridge at market, so this is effectively operating-DCF + listed-stake sum-of-parts. reported_fcf = FY2025 OCF 20,996 - full capex 2,716 (PPE 1,208 + CIP 1,297 + intangibles 145 + land use rights 66); the Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow (19,577) uses a narrower capex of 1,419. last_fcf = 18,280 - SBC 324 - interest received 1,581 = 16,375; under the lease treatment a further RMB4,700m of lease payments and ~RMB2.1bn of NCI profit share come out of the projected flows, which is why the component-built year-1 owner FCF is ~RMB10bn, not 16bn. Interest income is stripped because net cash (~RMB37.8bn) is >2x the FCF base. Government subsidies (RMB2,780m FY2025, 3.5% of revenue, in 'other net income') are left inside adj EBITDA in base/bull and partly faded in bear. Share of associates' profit (Amer Sports, RMB1,203m FY2025) is excluded from the flows; the stake is in the bridge at market. Net debt is at 30 June 2026: cash 16,994 + fixed deposits >3m 45,317 + pledged 290 = 62,601; less bank loans 3,849 + financing bills 9,000 + 2029 CB at principal 11,914 (carrying 10,639) = 24,763. The June cash balance carries some H1 seasonal working-capital inflow; Dec-2025 net cash on the company's own definition was RMB31.7bn.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 24.1% diverges >30% from revenue 3yr CAGR 14.3%. Book value has been inflated by non-operating Amer Sports gains (RMB1.6bn listing dilution gain FY2024, RMB2.1bn placing gain FY2024, RMB1.5bn placing gain H1 FY2026) and the share of associate profit, so equity CAGR overstates operating growth; the revenue CAGR is selected instead. EPS CAGR is distorted the same way (FY2024 EPS 5.41 includes RMB3.7bn of one-off gains).
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs end FY2025 (3yr from FY2022, 5yr from FY2020). Owner-FCF series = CSV FreeCashFlow - SBC - interest income: FY2020 6,368; FY2022 10,283; FY2023 17,401; FY2024 12,597; FY2025 17,672. Owner-FCF CAGRs sit ~1pp below reported, so SBC is not eating the growth (SBC is 0.4% of revenue); the gap is interest income on the growing cash pile. Revenue growth includes acquisitions (JACK WOLFSKIN consolidated from 2025); organic growth was lower -- H1 FY2026 ANTA brand +4.8%, FILA +6.1%, all other brands +44.2%.

base.narrative: FY2026 +11% (H1 +12.9% incl. a full half of JACK WOLFSKIN; ANTA and FILA mid-single-digit), decelerating to 3% by year 10. Pre-IFRS-16 adj EBITDA margin held near FY2025's 32.1%, inching to 32.5% on mix toward DESCENTE/KOLON (73% gross margin). Capex elevated near-term on the RMB8.3bn commitment book (industrial park, logistics), fading to 3%. Leakage rises to 40% as the NCI-heavy outdoor brands grow fastest.

scenario_narratives.base: ANTA brand grows low-to-mid single digit in a deflationary China mass market, defending share against Li Ning, Xtep and 361 Degrees through value pricing and kids/outlet channels; FILA keeps mid-single-digit growth with stable ~68% gross margins in premium sports-fashion; DESCENTE and KOLON SPORT carry group growth on the premium-outdoor boom but decelerate from 40%+ as the category matures; JACK WOLFSKIN's revitalisation is slow and roughly margin-neutral. Government subsidies persist at ~3% of revenue. Amer Sports and the pending PUMA stake are valued at market, not on synergy.
scenario_narratives.bull: China discretionary demand recovers with stimulus and the outdoor/premium mix shift continues: DESCENTE and KOLON sustain 25%+ growth for several years, FILA re-accelerates, overseas expansion (Southeast Asia, Middle East, US via the Amer network) and a revitalised JACK WOLFSKIN add a second growth engine, and PUMA as an associate opens global sourcing and distribution synergies. Operating leverage and DTC efficiency lift pre-lease EBITDA margin to 33.5% and lease cost dilutes as sales per store rise.
scenario_narratives.bear: China sportswear enters a prolonged price war: the ANTA brand stagnates as domestic rivals and Nike/Adidas discount, FILA's fashion cycle rolls over as it did in 2022 (FILA has a history of sharp reversals), the outdoor boom fades and DESCENTE/KOLON growth collapses to mid-single digits, and local-government subsidies (RMB2.8bn, ~14% of operating profit) are cut. Inventory builds force discounting; pre-lease EBITDA margin falls ~3pp to 29%. Capital allocation to Amer/PUMA is at premium prices with weak returns.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 20% from the 15% house default because China consumer deflation, a domestic price war and dependence on discretionary local-government subsidies are live, observable risks rather than tail events. Base 50%: H1 FY2026 (+12.9% revenue, +16% operating profit) tracks it. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs both a China demand recovery and successful international execution (JACK WOLFSKIN, PUMA) at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ANTA is valued as an operating business plus two listed stakes. The operating DCF charges leases as an operating cost, folds the ~15% minority share into a combined leakage rate, strips interest income, and values the operating flows at a 10% RMB cost of equity; the Amer Sports stake and the pending PUMA stake are marked to market and added with net cash. Much of the gap between price and value is the market applying a China-consumer discount the 10% WACC only partly captures; the required-return table shows what IRR today's price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: China discretionary consumption and sportswear price competition (ANTA brand only +4.8% in H1 FY2026)
Government subsidies (RMB2,780m FY2025, ~3.5% of revenue) inside operating profit could be cut
Amer Sports and PUMA stakes carry market and FX risk; together RMB47bn of bridge value, roughly a quarter of the market cap
PUMA bought at EUR35 vs EUR24 market; capital allocation to premium-priced minority stakes
Part of the cash sits in non-wholly-owned subsidiaries and is not fully attributable; June cash includes H1 seasonal inflow
2029 CB converts at HKD99.80; in the bull case the count rises ~4.4% (treated here as debt at principal)
RMB/HKD FX: per-share values move one-for-one with CNYHKD
